newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Shots ring out in Zaire behind force commander.
newsitem.headline: Shots ring out in Zaire behind force commander.

text.p: Refugees, aid workers and journalists fled from the eastern Zairean town of Sake on Thursday when gunshots rang out, shortly after the Canadian commander of a planned intervention force had driven by.

Lieutenant-General Maurice Baril had just driven through Sake in a convoy of vehicles after talks with rebel Zaireans in Goma, near the border with Rwanda, but a Reuters correspondent said the shots did not appear to have been aimed at him.
Earlier, the correspondent had seen around 10 truckloads of rebel Zairean troops drive into the hills above Sake.
None of the people who fled away from Sake towards Goma were injured. Later the scene was quiet but tense, the correspondent said.

Several carloads of journalists had earlier been stopped from following Baril at Sake. They had trailed him from Goma, where he had refused to comment after leaving a palace where he had been due to hold talks with rebel Zairean leader Laurent Kabila.
Baril's aides refused comment after the meeting, even declining to confirm he had met Kabila, but they said he would speak to reporters later on Thursday at the Rwandan border.
